title: Every run: word is also a glob matched against the project root, and a run: of only spaces runs the invocation's own arguments as the command
body:
## Summary

**`run:` is split into words unquoted (D1), and every word is then also a glob pattern matched against the project root, which nothing documents. And a `run:` of nothing but spaces splits to no words, so devbin runs the arguments typed after the command as the command itself, exit 0.**

Measured 2026-09-17 10:21Z at `c260eec`, through the real dispatcher, in a project installed with `bin/devbin install --into <tmp> --force`, with empty `alpha.md` and `beta.md` at its root:

```yaml
project:
  name: globprobe
commands:
  probe:
    summary: option-level probes
    options:
      control:
        summary: an ordinary run
        run: echo control-ran
      words:
        summary: prints its words
        run: printf [%s]\n *.md
      nomatch:
        summary: a glob that matches nothing
        run: printf [%s]\n *.nomatch
      blank:
        summary: a run of only space
        run: "   "
  globcmd:
    summary: command-level glob
    run: printf [%s]\n *.md
  blankcmd:
    summary: command-level blank run
    run: "   "
```

```
--- option run: echo control-ran (CONTROL)   (invoked as: devbin probe control)
rc=0
control-ran
--- option run: printf [%s]\n *.md, with alpha.md and beta.md at the root   (invoked as: devbin probe words)
rc=0
[alpha.md]
[beta.md]
--- option run: printf [%s]\n *.nomatch   (invoked as: devbin probe nomatch)
rc=0
[*.nomatch]
--- option run: "   "   (invoked as: devbin probe blank echo EXECUTED-AS-THE-COMMAND)
rc=0
EXECUTED-AS-THE-COMMAND
--- command run: printf [%s]\n *.md   (invoked as: devbin globcmd)
rc=0
[alpha.md]
[beta.md]
--- command run: "   "   (invoked as: devbin blankcmd echo EXECUTED-AS-THE-COMMAND)
rc=0
EXECUTED-AS-THE-COMMAND
--- command run: printf [%s]\n *.md, after the root's .md files became gamma.md alone   (invoked as: devbin globcmd)
rc=0
[gamma.md]
```

## Why it matters

- **The command a declared `run:` produces depends on the files at the project root when it runs.** `globcmd` ran `printf [%s]\n alpha.md beta.md`, and after those two became `gamma.md`, `printf [%s]\n gamma.md`: one config, two commands. A word that matches nothing passes through as written (`[*.nomatch]`), so neither case says anything.
- **`docs/configuration.md` (line 319) says `run:` "is expanded unquoted and never `eval`'d" and that "Word splitting is wanted".** It says nothing of globs, so a reader takes the expansion to be word splitting alone.
- **A `run:` of only spaces is not empty to `[ -n "$run" ]`** (`lib/resolve` 689 and 864), splits to no words, and `$run "$@"` or `exec $run "$@"` then runs whatever the user typed after the command, as the command, exit 0, with no message. Measured with `echo`; nothing limits it to `echo`.

## Found

2026-09-17, by critic-shell reviewing ST0007 WP-02's `notes.run`, which is expanded the same way (WP-02 refuses a blank `notes.run` itself). Measured by dc at option level at `f34753f`, and at option and command level at `c260eec` (above).

## The sites

- `lib/resolve` 754 to 766: an option's `run:` under the gate runner (`-- $run ...`).
- `lib/resolve` 780 to 783: an option's `run:` (`$run "$@"`).
- `lib/resolve` 875 to 885: a command's `run:` under the gate runner.
- `lib/resolve` 891 to 892: a command's `run:` (`exec $run "$@"`).
- The emptiness tests before them: `lib/resolve` 689 and 864.
- Since ST0007 WP-02 (`5f4d898`): `_notes_command_out` in `lib/release.notes`, for `notes.run`.

## The shape of a fix

- **One ruling for every `run:` site.** Either split without globbing and say so in `docs/configuration.md`, or keep globbing and document that every word is a pattern matched at the project root. Before ruling, read every estate's `run:` values for `*`, `?` and `[`: a project relying on globbing today breaks under the first choice.
- **One helper that turns a `run:` value into words**, used by every site, so the ruling has one home rather than five.
- **Refuse a `run:` with no words, naming the key**, in validation and at the site, since `doctor` is not on the dispatch path (0080's first residual).

## Arms a fix needs

- A `run:` word holding `*`, `?` or `[...]` reaches the command as the ruling says, with a matching file present at the root, at option and command level, and for `notes.run`.
- A `run:` of only spaces is refused at option and command level, naming the key, and the arguments after the command never run.
- A mutation restoring globbing at any one site, or removing the refusal, goes red.

## Routing (hv, 2026-09-17)

- **vc runs the census first**, approved by hv in vc's session on vc's proposal: every estate's `run:` values read for `*`, `?` and `[`, read-only, as the shape above says to do before ruling.
- **The ruling on globbing is hv's and is not yet made.** It follows the census.
- **vc builds, after ST0007 WP-03, and dc reviews.** dc measured it, and the `notes.run` site is dc's WP-02 code.

## Census (vc, 2026-09-17)

Read-only, at devbin `d6cb655`, 14:50Z. **The population is 30 installs**: the 29 `bin/devbin fleet audit` listed (17 estates and 12 vendored deps) and devbin's own tree. Every config was read with devbin's own parser (`cfg_load` and `cfg_dump` from `lib/config`), not grep or PyYAML, and all 30 parsed. Each value under a key whose last segment is `run` or `restore` was split into words as the sites split it, and each word holding `*`, `?` or `[` was expanded at that install's root as the sites expand it, with no glob option set, since devbin sets none. The census was run first against a fixture: `*.md` beside two .md files found 2 matches, `*.nomatch` found none, and a missing library exited 2.

| Values read                    | Count    |
| ------------------------------ | -------- |
| option-level `run:`            | 86       |
| command-level `run:`           | 16       |
| `commands.fullcycle.restore`   | 1        |
| `release.notes.run`            | 0        |
| installs declaring any of them | 26 of 30 |

**Exactly one word in the fleet globs, and it matches today.**

| Install | Key                               | Value             | Word         | At the root today                                   |
| ------- | --------------------------------- | ----------------- | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Utilz   | `commands.test.options.shell.run` | `bats opt/*/test` | `opt/*/test` | 16 matches, one `test` directory per tool in `opt/` |

- **Under "split without globbing", Utilz breaks:** `test shell` hands bats the literal `opt/*/test`, which names no path, so `test shell` and `test all` fail there, and so does Utilz's `fullcycle` once 0083 reaches it. Under "keep globbing and document it", nothing in the fleet changes.
- **No `run:` in the fleet is blank.** The fewest words any value splits to is one, so the refusal the fix adds changes no install's behaviour today.
- **Widened to every key**, 9 values hold one of the three characters. Besides Utilz's `run:`, five are `args:` usage hints and one is a `summary:`, which are help text and never run. The other two are `project.referent` at Gtools and Lamplight, which `bin/devbin` runs through `eval` by design, so their `[` is shell syntax under a different rule from `run:`.

## Ruling (hv, 2026-09-17)

- **Keep globbing, and document it.** hv ruled in vc's session, taking vc's recommendation after the census. A `run:` word stays a glob pattern, matched in the directory the command runs from: the project root, or for `notes.run` the root it answers for. `docs/configuration.md` says so. Nothing in the fleet changes, and Utilz's `bats opt/*/test` keeps its matches.
- **The rest of the fix stands.**
  - One helper turns a `run:` value into words at every site, `notes.run` included, so the ruling has one home.
  - A `run:` with no words is refused naming the key, in validation and at the site.
  - The arms read the ruling: a word holding `*`, `?` or `[...]` is expanded at every site with a matching file present, so a mutation that stops globbing at any one site goes red.
- **Sequencing: vc builds it now, ahead of ST0007 WP-03, and dc reviews.** hv, 2026-09-17: "crack on and get them closed out". WP-03 was claimed and started at `bde9812`, with nothing built yet, and resumes after.

## Fixed 2026-09-17 -- one reading of a declared command line (vc), reviewed by dc

Fixed across `169a349` (the build), `c635e77` and `e3f1231` (what three other readers found in it), on hv's ruling of 2026-09-17: **the globbing is KEPT and documented, one helper holds the rule, and a command line with no words in it is refused naming its key.**

**The ruling came after a census, not after an argument.** Every `run:`, `restore:` and `notes.run` value across all 30 installs was read with devbin's own parser: exactly one word in the fleet actually globs -- Utilz's, matching 16 directories -- and no value anywhere would be broken by the refusal. Removing the globbing would have been a silent behaviour change for a working project; documenting it costs a paragraph.

**The eight sites, censused by shape rather than by spelling.** shfmt's syntax tree over all 43 tracked runtime shell files, with a control fixture of six known shapes and three negatives run first, found eight calls whose command word is an unquoted expansion: an option's `run:` bare (`lib/resolve`) and under a gate, a command's exec'd and under a gate, `commands.fullcycle.restore`, `release.notes.run`, and the two that run devbin's own catalogue lines (`lib/gatecmd`, `lib/cmd/check`). So how a command line becomes words was stated eight times, each reading the caller's `IFS` and whatever glob options the process happened to carry. `bin/devbin`'s `eval` of `project.referent` is a different rule and out of scope. dc's independent census, through shellcheck's SC2086 over the gate's 45-file corpus, agrees on all eight.

**`run_words` in `lib/helpers` is now the one reading.** It splits on space, tab and newline whatever the caller's `IFS`; matches every word where the caller stands, which each site makes the directory the command runs from -- the project root, or for `notes.run` the root it answers about; passes a word matching nothing through as written; never `eval`s; and refuses a value with no words, naming its key. It pins `set -f` and the six glob shopts for the split alone and puts them back, so an inherited `SHELLOPTS=noglob` or `BASHOPTS=nullglob:dotglob` cannot quietly change what a declared line runs -- both measured on bash 5.3, turning globbing off entirely and dropping a word that matches nothing.

**The reported behaviour, both halves.** A `run:` of nothing but spaces split to no words, after which `$run "$@"` ran the arguments typed after the command AS the command, at exit 0 and with no message, at option and command level alike. It is refused now at the site and in `cfg_validate`, which is what `doctor` reads -- both ends, because doctor is not on the dispatch path and the sites are not on doctor's. `run: ""` is refused too: `cfg_has` replaces `[ -n "$run" ]` at option level, command level and for `restore`, so a declared empty line no longer falls through to devbin's own catalogue line, which it did silently.

**Documented** on five surfaces -- `docs/configuration.md`, `README.md`, `docs/migration.md`, `usage-rules.md` and `lib/config.reference.yaml` -- and the gate log's own source line now names the rule rather than word splitting alone.

**Verification.** 29 new arms, each seen red first (11 in a new `tests/unit/runwords.bats`, 11 in `helpers.bats`, 3 in `fullcycle.bats`, 2 in `config.bats`, 2 in `release.bats`); no existing arm deleted. **Full suite at `e3f1231`: 1372 of 1372, 0 failures.** One of them is dc's measurement in a single line: a `[%s]` word matches a file named `s`, so a printf FORMAT becomes a filename. Full suite green at the commit. **Held by mutation, not by the arms' own say-so.** 15 mutants in `git archive` exports, each anchor verified to appear exactly once, each applied to a fresh copy of a pristine export, tree-diffed before (exactly one file differs) and after the restore (nothing differs). Two harness controls ran first, because a campaign in exports proves nothing if the exports read the shared tree's `lib`: a pristine export is 11/11 green, and an export whose `run_words` always refuses goes 10 of 11 red -- the second is the half that carries the proof. Every mutant was killed at the arm meant for it, after one of them was not: **a bypass of the `notes.run` run site SURVIVED**, because the old expansion globbed at the root too and `IFS` has been pinned locally at that site since before 0082. The glob state is what separates the two readings, and the arm that now holds it drives the site under an inherited `SHELLOPTS=noglob`. The survivor was the campaign's most useful result.

**Declared limits.**
- At `lib/cmd/check` no input devbin ships tells `run_words` from the old expansion: no catalogue line holds a glob character or is blank, and bash never imports `IFS` from the environment (measured). That site moved for one rule, not for a behaviour.
- A command-line key added to the schema without joining `_cfg_path_command_line` is validated as ordinary text. Nothing catches that but a reader.
- **An INTEGER output array is not refused and the guard cannot refuse it**: `declare -ia w` carries a name that IS a name, so the defect is the attribute rather than the spelling. Measured on bash 5.3, and wrong in both directions in the comment that used to claim it refused: under `set +u` the word `abc` coerces silently to `(0)`, so the caller runs the command `0`; under devbin's own `set -euo pipefail` the arithmetic on an unset name kills the shell outright. No site passes an integer array, and closing it would mean reading `declare -p` output as a string.
- `GLOBIGNORE` and `GLOBSORT` are deliberately not pinned, and **not pinning is the only correct answer rather than the convenient one**: bash runs their hooks on ASSIGNMENT, so once either is touched the inert state cannot be restored by any assignment -- save it, unset it, write the same bytes back, and it comes back active (dc, measured). A pin would be a one-way door for the whole process. A test holds devbin to assigning neither.
- **`notes_select` validates through `has_words` and has no arm, deliberately.** There is provably no input separating the two readers there: the only caller cd's to the project root first, and with `nullglob` unset a word matching nothing passes through, so the array is non-empty exactly when `has_words` is true. It is a contract fix -- `lib/release.notes`'s header says every verb takes the root it reads and depends on nothing else, and `notes_select` takes no root -- and an arm for it would be an arm that cannot go red.
- The census is a method, not a test: a ninth site added later is caught by review. A source arm over bash's own parser was prototyped and dropped -- it missed `exec $run` on macOS, because BSD awk has no `\<`.

**What `c635e77` added, all of it found by a reader other than the author.** critic-shell found `notes_select` validating by globbing, against a comment in the same commit. dc found that the split, pinned between `shopt -u` and `shopt -s`, left the caller's glob options unset for the rest of its life if bash refused the assignment into the caller's array -- a readonly target, or `declare -ia` and a non-arithmetic word -- so the split now lands in a local and is copied out after the restore. Both readers found the nameref shadowing: a caller passing `IFS`, `_rw_o` or `_rw_on` as the output array name had it shadowed by the helper's own local, so the words died with the local and `run_words` returned 0 with the caller's array never set -- which is 0082 itself, rebuilt inside the helper written to kill it. It is refused now with status 2, a programming error where 1 means the config's line held no words. No site could reach either; both were traps for the next caller.

**And `e3f1231`, which is the sharpest of them.** The name guard `c635e77` added was a BLACKLIST of the helper's own locals, and dc drove the hole beside it: when `$1` is not a shell variable name at all, `local -n` fails with bash's own `invalid variable name for name reference`, EXECUTION FALLS THROUGH, and `run_words` returns 0 with the caller's array never set -- after which `"${words[@]}" "$@"` is the empty command line that runs the arguments typed after the command, at exit 0. **That is this issue's own defect, rebuilt inside the helper written to kill it, one line below a guard watching a different door.** Measured at rc=0: `2bad`, `a b`, `a-b`, `-x`, `a;b`; `arr[0]` reached the copy and returned 1, reporting a good name as a config line with no words. The question is asked positively now, through `is_identifier` -- **and not through a new regex**, because `assert_identifier` already owned that charset and a second spelling of "is a name" is the divergence Highlander is about. One predicate, two refusal policies: `assert_identifier` dies naming the rule broken, `run_words` warns and returns 2, since nothing in the release library may die.

**And two arms that could not fail.** `builtins.bats`'s "a declared option runs at the project root, not the caller's directory" drove through a helper that cd's to the root before invoking devbin, so the caller was never anywhere else; it now invokes devbin from the nested directory by absolute path, proven red with the cd dropped. **One of `c635e77`'s own new arms was also vacuous on first writing** -- it went green, and green again when the hardening was reverted to check it, because the reversion moved the failing assignment to before the pinned window where there was nothing yet to leak. A faithful reversion fails as predicted. A red-first check is worth exactly what its broken input is worth.
